animations/list-of-supported-animations-.title: List of ScrollJs Built-in CSS Animations
animations/list-of-supported-animations-.description: Looking to skip the hassle of writing custom animation classes? ScrollJs has your back with a set of built-in CSS animations ready to go out of the box! Just plug and play — and yes, they’re smooth as butter.

getting-started/initialization.description: After adding ScrollJs via CDN or package manager, you can start using it right away. The library exports a ScrollObserver class — just instantiate it to begin observing elements.

intro.description: What are the benefits of using ScrollJs?

live-demos/disconnect-method-demo.title: disconnect() Method Demo
live-demos/disconnect-method-demo.description: The disconnect() method is used to remove all active observers, effectively stopping any elements from being watched or animated. This is useful when you want to clean up and prevent further animation triggers.

live-demos/observe-method-demos.title: observe() Method Demos
live-demos/observe-method-demos.description: The observe() method is the core of ScrollJs, allowing you to trigger animations when elements enter the viewport. Below are two usage examples:

live-demos/unobserve-method-demo.title: unobserve() Method Demo
live-demos/unobserve-method-demo.description: Here's a demo usage of the unobserve() method, super straight forward to use!

methods/disconnect-method.title: disconnect() Method
methods/disconnect-method.description: The disconnect() method is your master switch 🔌 — it stops observing all elements that were previously passed to the observe() method.

methods/observe-method.title: observe() Method
methods/observe-method.description: The observe() method is the most important method provided by the ScrollObserver() class. It's use to observe elements position on the page and add an animation when the element being observed enter or leave the viewport.

methods/unobserve-method.title: unobserve() Method
methods/unobserve-method.description: The unobserve() method is useful when you want to stop observing a specific element — even if it's part of a group being observed (e.g., elements with the same class name).

playground.title: ScrollJs Playground
playground.description: Welcome to the ScrollJs Playground, a fully interactive space where you can edit code live, test different animation classes, and experiment with ScrollObserver methods in real time.
